mainTopic: פטר חמור with a נכרי's share, and whether רבי יהודה permits selling a fetus to a נכרי
overview: מסכת בכורות opens with the משנה of פרק הלוקח עובר חמורו. The משנה lists five cases where a Jew and a נכרי are both involved with a donkey or its fetus, and rules that in every one the newborn is exempt from בכורה, because the פסוק says 'בישראל'. The גמרא then explains why each case is needed. Selling and giving an animal בקבלה are listed so we do not think חז"ל would penalize the Jew with a קנס. Partnership is listed to reject רבי יהודה, who obligates a partnership with a גוי in בכורה. Receiving an animal is listed only as the pair of the giving case. Next the גמרא quotes a משנה in עבודה זרה where רבי יהודה permits selling a broken animal to a נכרי, and asks whether he would also permit selling a fetus. A first proof from our משנה is rejected, because the משנה often leaves out רבי יהודה's disagreements. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא of רבי יהודה on receivership as a second proof, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: Gentile involvement exempts a firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five ways a Jew and a נכרי can share involvement in a donkey. In all of them the firstborn donkey is exempt from בכורה, based on the word 'בישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who buys the unborn foal of a gentile's donkey, or sells his own donkey's unborn foal to a gentile (even though he is not allowed to do this), or becomes partners with a gentile, or takes a donkey from a gentile to raise, or gives his donkey to a gentile to raise: in all these cases the foal is exempt from firstborn laws. The verse says 'in Israel', which means only among Jews and not among others.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives five cases where a נכרי has some ownership or stake in a donkey or its fetus. It rules that in every one of them the newborn donkey is not treated as a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the פסוק 'הקדשתי לי כל בכור בישראל'. The obligation of בכורה applies only when the animal belongs entirely to a Jew, so any share held by a נכרי removes it. The phrase 'אף על פי שאינו רשאי' notes in passing that selling a large animal (בהמה גסה) to a נכרי is forbidden. Even so, once the sale is done, the foal is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the text being discussed)
Fetus; an unborn animal
A non-Jew
One who enters a partnership
In receivership: giving an animal to someone to raise in exchange for a share of the young
Exempt from the laws of a firstborn animal

steps.confusionAlert: 'אף על פי שאינו רשאי' does not mean the sale fails. Selling a large animal to a נכרי is forbidden, but once it happens the sale works, and the foal is exempt from בכורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic rule for the whole chapter: בכורה requires full Jewish ownership.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר חֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁל נָכְרִי,
phrases.english: Mishnah: One who buys the fetus of a gentile's donkey,
and one who sells [his donkey's fetus] to him,
phrases.notes: 'לו' refers to the gentile.

phrases.english: even though he is not permitted [to do so],
phrases.notes: It is forbidden to sell a large animal to a non-Jew.

phrases.english: one who enters a partnership with him,
and one who receives [a donkey] from him [to raise],
and one who gives [his donkey] to him in receivership:
[the animal] is exempt from firstborn status,
as it is stated: 'in Israel',
but not among others.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר חֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁל נָכְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the מסכת and the פרק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any involvement of a נכרי in ownership of the donkey or its fetus exempts the firstborn from בכורה, because the פסוק says 'בישראל'.

steps.title: Why does the משנה list so many cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs all five cases if they all teach the same principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need all of these cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists so many examples of the same rule. This question sets up the next steps, where the גמרא will explain why each case is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that a משנה does not repeat itself for no reason. If one case already teaches that a נכרי's involvement exempts the animal, the other cases look extra. The גמרא will now show that each case adds something new.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
All these
Why do I need it? (asks what a phrase adds)

phrases.english: Gemara: Why do I need all these [cases]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the long list in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each extra case in the משנה adds beyond the basic principle.

steps.title: Selling is needed even though buying was listed
steps.stepSummary: The case of selling is needed. Otherwise we might think חז"ל would penalize a Jew who sells to a נכרי by keeping the foal obligated in בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are all needed. If the משנה had taught only the buyer, I would have said he is exempt because he is bringing the animal into a state of holiness. But a seller removes it from holiness, so I might say חז"ל should penalize him. The משנה teaches us that he is exempt too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the cases are necessary. It explains why the case of a seller cannot simply be learned from the case of a buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew who buys from a נכרי moves the animal into Jewish hands, so it becomes subject to Jewish laws like resting on שבת. He has done nothing wrong, so there is no reason to penalize him, and the exemption from the פסוק simply applies. A Jew who sells to a נכרי takes the animal out of that קדושה, so we might expect a קנס that keeps the obligation in place. The משנה teaches that there is no such penalty: the exemption comes from the פסוק, not from how the owner behaved.

keyTerms.meaning: They are necessary
I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
Holy or protected status (here, being under Jewish laws such as resting on שבת)
Removes or cancels
Let us penalize him (from קנס)
It teaches us (introduces the actual lesson)

phrases.english: They are necessary,
for if it had taught [only] the buyer,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ לִקְדוּשָּׁה,
phrases.english: I would have said [he is exempt] because he brings it into sanctity,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מוֹכֵר דְּקָא מַפְקַע לַהּ מִקְּדוּשָּׁה —
phrases.english: but a seller, who removes it from sanctity,
I might say we should penalize him,
[therefore] it teaches us [that he is exempt too].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the extra cases
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seller case is needed so we do not think חז"ל penalize a seller by keeping the foal obligated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A seller who removes the animal from קדושה deserves a קנס, so his foal would stay obligated in בכורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: No קנס applies. The foal is exempt in the seller's case as well.

steps.title: Why is the partnership case needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case of a partnership with a נכרי adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need 'one who enters a partnership with him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, a partnership with a נכרי, and asks why it was needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know that full ownership by a נכרי exempts the animal, a partial share seems to follow obviously. So the גמרא asks what new point the partnership case teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: And one who partners with him (quoting the משנה)

phrases.english: And 'one who enters a partnership with him': why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through the משנה case by case

steps.title: Partnership is listed to reject רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The partnership case is there to rule against רבי יהודה, who holds that an animal shared with a גוי is obligated in בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude the view of רבי יהודה, who says that a partnership with a gentile is obligated in firstborn laws. The משנה teaches us that it is exempt from firstborn laws.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the משנה mentions partnership on purpose. It is taking a stand against רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a partnership with a גוי is obligated in בכורה. The משנה's list follows the opposing view: any share held by a נכרי exempts the animal. So this case is not extra. It decides a real מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (to reject a different opinion)
A תנא, here holding a minority view
Partnership with a non-Jew
Is obligated

steps.whatToRemember: Each case in the משנה is needed. Selling is listed so we do not think חז"ל penalize the seller. Partnership is listed to reject רבי יהודה, who obligates a partnership with a גוי in בכורה.

phrases.english: To exclude [the view] of Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: a partnership with a gentile is obligated in firstborn status,
it teaches us that it is exempt from firstborn status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the partnership case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The partnership case rejects רבי יהודה's view and establishes that a partnership with a גוי is exempt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying an opposing opinion that the case rejects

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the case of the receiver?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the case of a Jew who receives a donkey from a נכרי to raise.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the case of 'one who receives', why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues checking each case in the משנה. Now it asks about the case of מקבל, where a Jew takes a נכרי's donkey to raise in exchange for a share of the offspring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the נכרי still owns the mother and has a share in the offspring. That looks just like the partnership (שותפות) case already explained, so this case seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who receives an animal to raise in exchange for a share of the young
Why do I need it? (Why is this case stated?)

phrases.english: And the one who receives, why do I need it?
phrases.notes: A Jew who receives a נכרי's donkey to raise, in exchange for part of the offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of 'why do I need this case' questions, moving on from partnership to מקבל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the case of מקבל add beyond the partnership case?

steps.title: It is stated to match its mirror case
steps.stepSummary: The מקבל case teaches nothing new. It is stated only because the משנה wants to teach the opposite case, נותן בקבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wants to teach 'and one who gives to him in receivership.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מקבל case is there only for the sake of style. It forms a pair with the next case, where the Jew gives his donkey to the נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא admits the מקבל case adds no new law. The משנה states it so that the pair is complete: receiving from a נכרי and giving to a נכרי. The real question now moves to the second case.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it wants to teach (a case is stated only to go along with another case)
One who gives his animal to another person to raise, for a share of the young

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a new law in the מקבל case. The גמרא openly says it is there only as a partner to the next case.

phrases.english: Because it wants to teach
phrases.notes: The case is included only for the sake of a parallel case.

phrases.english: and one who gives to him in receivership.
phrases.notes: The Jew gives his own donkey to the נכרי to raise.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מקבל case is stated only to go along with its mirror case, נותן בקבלה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the case of giving to a נכרי to raise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks what the case of נותן בקבלה adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the case of 'one who gives to him in receivership', why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 7 pushed the real point onto the נותן בקבלה case. So now the גמרא asks what that case itself teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the Jew owns the mother and gives a נכרי a share in the offspring. A share for the נכרי already exempts the foal, as we know from the partnership case. So this case also seems to repeat that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: An arrangement to raise someone else's animal in exchange for a share of its young

phrases.english: And the one who gives to him in receivership, why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 7, which said the real point is in the נותן case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea does נותן בקבלה teach?

steps.title: No penalty, even though the mother belongs to the Jew
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought חז"ל would penalize the Jew. The mother is his, and people might confuse this case with one where the foal really is obligated. The משנה teaches that there is no penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since the main animal belongs to the Jew, we should penalize him, in case people confuse it with another animal. So it teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the נותן case is needed to rule out a possible קנס (penalty) on the Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the mother animal is fully the Jew's, people might confuse this case with a different one. In that case the Jew gives his animal to a נכרי with no share in the young, and the firstborn is obligated. So we might have thought חז"ל would obligate the foal here too, as a fence. The משנה teaches that they did not make such a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
It might have entered your mind to say (the 'I would have thought' view)
The main animal, here meaning the mother
Let us penalize him (a rabbinic קנס)
To be confused or mixed up with
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: Every case in the משנה has a reason. Selling and נותן בקבלה rule out a קנס. Partnership rules against רבי יהודה. מקבל is just the partner of נותן.

phrases.english: It was necessary; it might have entered your mind to say:
since the main animal belongs to the Jew,
phrases.notes: The mother is fully owned by the Jew.

phrases.english: we should penalize him, lest it come to be confused
phrases.notes: The penalty would be treating the foal as a בכור.

phrases.english: with another animal,
phrases.notes: An animal handed to a נכרי with no share in the young, whose firstborn is obligated.

phrases.english: so it teaches us (that we do not).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8, using the same 'no קנס' idea as step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case teaches that there is no penalty, even though the mother belongs to the Jew and people might confuse cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Penalize the Jew by obligating the foal, because of possible confusion with another animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: No penalty; the foal is exempt.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about selling large animals to a נכרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from עבודה זרה. רבי יהודה permits selling a broken animal to a נכרי, and בן בתירא permits selling a horse.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: רבי יהודה permits selling a broken animal, and בן בתירא permits selling a horse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from another מסכת. This is a setup for the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general it is forbidden to sell large animals to a נכרי, because he will work them on שבת. רבי יהודה permits selling a שבורה (a broken animal), since it cannot work. בן בתירא permits selling a horse, since riding is not forbidden מן התורה.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Permits
A broken or injured animal that cannot work
Horse, used for riding rather than work

steps.whyThisMatters: Our משנה mentions selling a fetus (עובר) to a נכרי. The גמרא will try to use that line to answer the question raised in the next step, but that attempt is rejected in Steps 13-14.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן הָתָם: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בַּשְּׁבוּרָה,
phrases.english: We learned there: Rabbi Yehuda permits a broken animal,
phrases.notes: From עבודה זרה; this refers to selling to a נכרי.

phrases.english: Ben Beteira permits a horse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic that will later connect to our משנה's case of selling a fetus.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה permits selling a broken animal to a נכרי, and בן בתירא permits selling a horse.

steps.title: Would רבי יהודה allow selling a fetus?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה would also permit selling a fetus. Maybe a fetus counts as 'broken' because it cannot work. Or maybe only a damaged animal counts, while a fetus is normal and will grow up to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what would רבי יהודה say about a fetus? Does he permit a broken animal because it cannot work, so a fetus counts as broken too? Or does a broken animal count only because it is not in its normal state? A fetus is in its normal state, so maybe it is not 'broken'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a בעיא (an open question) about how far רבי יהודה's leniency goes. It lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what makes a שבורה permitted. If the reason is simply 'cannot work now', a fetus is also permitted. If the reason is 'damaged and not its natural state', a fetus is normal and will grow into a working animal, so it would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question)
Fetus
The reason
Or perhaps (introduces the other side)
Its normal way or natural state

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree a fetus cannot work right now. The argument is only about why רבי יהודה permits a broken animal: because it cannot work, or because it is defective.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עוּבָּר מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: It was asked of them: a fetus, what would Rabbi Yehuda say to me?
phrases.notes: About selling a fetus to a נכרי.

phrases.english: The reason Rabbi Yehuda permits there

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דִּשְׁבוּרָה, עוּבָּר נָמֵי שָׁבוּר הוּא.
phrases.english: is because it is broken; a fetus is also 'broken'.
phrases.notes: First side: it cannot work, so it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: שְׁבוּרָה לָאו הַיְינוּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps: a broken animal is not in its normal state,
phrases.notes: Second side begins.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוּבָּר, כֵּיוָן דְּהַיְינוּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ, לָאו שָׁבוּר הוּא?
phrases.english: but a fetus, since this is its normal state, is not 'broken'?
phrases.notes: It will grow up and work, so it is not defective.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עוּבָּר מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the ruling of רבי יהודה quoted in step 10 extends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה's permission for a broken animal include a fetus? This depends on whether the reason is 'cannot work' or 'is defective'.

steps.title: A proof from the silence of our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer the question from our משנה. The משנה says selling a fetus to a נכרי is not permitted, and רבי יהודה is not recorded as arguing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And one who sells it to him, even though he is not permitted.' And רבי יהודה does not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for the question it just asked. Our משנה forbids selling a fetus to a נכרי, and no disagreement from רבי יהודה is mentioned. So it seems he agrees that it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether a fetus counts like a 'broken' animal, which רבי יהודה lets you sell. Our משנה says selling a fetus is אינו רשאי (not allowed). If רבי יהודה held otherwise, we would expect the משנה to record his argument. His silence suggests a fetus is NOT like a broken animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the formula that introduces a proof from a source
One who sells (here, the fetus of his donkey to a נכרי)
He is not permitted (to do this in the first place)
He does not argue / disagree

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: Opens a proof attempt.

phrases.english: 'And one who sells to him (the fetus)'
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה.

phrases.english: even though he is not permitted.
phrases.notes: The animal is exempt from בכורה, but the sale itself was forbidden.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda does not argue.
phrases.notes: The proof rests on his silence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question raised in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה forbids selling a fetus to a נכרי (a fetus is not like a broken animal).
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: 'והמוכר לו אף על פי שאינו רשאי', with no recorded argument from רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Silence also covers cases where he does argue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. The משנה also records no argument from רבי יהודה on the partnership cases, yet we would not say he agrees there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning: one who becomes a partner with him, one who receives from him, and one who gives to him in receivership, where the משנה does not mention רבי יהודה, would you also say that he does not argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof with a counter-question. If silence means agreement, then רבי יהודה would also agree to the משנה's other cases, and that cannot be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts animals owned in partnership with a נכרי from בכורה. Yet רבי יהודה holds that such animals ARE obligated, as the ברייתא in Step 15 will show. So the משנה's silence about רבי יהודה cannot mean he agrees. That breaks the logic of Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turns the other side's logic back on itself
One who becomes a partner (with a נכרי in an animal)
It teaches / it states (the משנה)
So too? (rhetorical: would you really say that?)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though this line ends with a question mark, it is not asking for information. It is a rhetorical challenge meant to knock down the proof.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
phrases.notes: Signals a counter-challenge.

phrases.english: one who becomes a partner with him,
phrases.notes: First partnership case in the משנה.

phrases.english: and one who receives (an animal) from him,
phrases.notes: Second case: the Jew raises the נכרי's animal for a share of the offspring.

phrases.english: and one who gives to him in receivership,
phrases.notes: Third case: the Jew gives his own animal to the נכרי to raise.

phrases.english: where it does not teach (that Rabbi Yehuda argues),
would you also say that he does not argue?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: obviously not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 12 by showing that its logic fails in parallel cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof drawn from the משנה's silence.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה often does not record רבי יהודה's arguments, so silence does not show that he agrees.

steps.title: He argues even though the משנה does not say so
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the rejection. In the partnership cases רבי יהודה argues even though the משנה does not record it, and the same may be true for selling a fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he argues, and the משנה simply does not mention it. Here too, he argues, and it does not mention it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its rejection. Our משנה just does not quote רבי יהודה, so we cannot learn his view on the fetus from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we know רבי יהודה disagrees on the partnership cases without the משנה saying so, the same could be true for the fetus case. The proof from Step 12 falls away. The question from Step 11 is not answered by this proof, so Step 15 brings a new source to try again.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: introduces the correct alternative
He argues, but it is not taught (not recorded)
Here too: applies the same idea to our case

phrases.english: Rather, he argues, but it is not taught.
phrases.notes: Applies to the partnership cases.

phrases.english: Here too, he argues, but it is not taught.
phrases.notes: Applies to selling the fetus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The silence of our משנה tells us nothing about רבי יהודה's view on selling a fetus, so the question is still open.
steps.whatToRemember: Proof #1 failed. A משנה not mentioning רבי יהודה does not mean he agrees.

steps.title: A new proof from a ברייתא: רבי יהודה on receivership cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with רבי יהודה's rulings on receiving an animal from a נכרי and on giving one to a נכרי in receivership. This sets up the next proof attempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, one who receives an animal from a נכרי and it gives birth: we assess its value, and he gives half its value to the כהן. And one who gives an animal to a נכרי in receivership, even though he is not permitted, is penalized up to ten times its value, and he gives its full value to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא of רבי יהודה as a new source for the question. It is setting up a proof, and the inference from it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא confirms what Step 13 assumed: רבי יהודה holds that a Jew's share in a jointly owned animal still carries בכורה. In the receiving case, the Jew pays the כהן for his half. In the giving case, חז"ל penalize him: he must buy out the נכרי's share, even at up to ten times its value, and give the full value to the כהן. The phrase 'אף על פי שאינו רשאי' here will be the key to the coming proof about the fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: They assess it at its value (set its price)
Half its value (the Jew's share)
They penalize (a rabbinic fine)
Up to ten times its value
Priest, who receives the value of the בכור

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא proves that רבי יהודה really does argue on the partnership cases in our משנה, which supports the rejection in Steps 13-14. It also gives the גמרא new material for the fetus question.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: New proof attempt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says,
one who receives an animal from a gentile, and it gave birth —
phrases.notes: The Jew raises it for a share in the offspring.

phrases.english: they assess it at its value,
and he gives half its value to the priest.
phrases.notes: His half is holy as a בכור.

phrases.english: And one who gives to him in receivership,
phrases.notes: The Jew's own animal is given to the נכרי to raise.

phrases.english: even though he is not permitted —
phrases.notes: The same phrase as in our משנה.

phrases.english: they penalize him up to ten times its value,
phrases.notes: He must buy out the נכרי's share, even at a high price.

phrases.english: and he gives its entire value to the priest.
phrases.notes: The penalty: the whole value goes to the כהן, not just half.
